lines.text: Introduction, section one. Why a second volume.
The first volume of Play Optimal Poker built its foundation on river play, where ranges are either polarized or condensed and the story usually ends with a single decision.
This second volume moves us backward through the hand, into the turn and the flop, where hands are still evolving and every choice you make is really a choice about several streets at once.
That difference matters more than it sounds, because on early streets a hand can be a bluff on one runout, a value bet on another, and a bluff-catcher on a third.
You cannot simply label a hand and move on; you have to think about how its role will change as new cards arrive.
That flexibility is the source of most of the complexity we will wade into together in the chapters ahead.
This book will still use scenarios to isolate ideas, but the scenarios will look and feel much more like real poker than the tiny toy games we solved in volume one.
You will learn to think in ranges rather than in single hands, and you will learn to build those ranges deliberately, one street at a time.

The metaphor we will keep returning to is construction: picking hands for a range is like picking players for a team, choosing pieces that complement each other and set up strong plays on future streets.
By the end of the book you should be able to reason about turn barreling, protection, leverage, and range construction with the same confidence that volume one gave you for river play.
